clue.text: Horribly bled? Ice is a sound measure

indicators.note: something done horribly is done badly, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gory question about bleeding and ice somehow turns into a statement about acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' rearranges the letters of BLED and ICE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit used to express the loudness of a noise.

clue.text: Waddle badly and drag, one's feet

indicators.note: a thing done badly is botched, so the word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone waddles clumsily and shuffles along slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges WADDLE, which simply swaps its W and first D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither and move slowly is to delay deliberately, the idiom of dragging one's feet.

clue.text: Joined prison after lag had meal

indicators.note: the prison word is placed after the convict word

parts.note: an old lag is a convict, a con
jug is slang for prison
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A convict who has just eaten is locked up with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugate as an adjective means coupled or joined together in pairs.

clue.text: Could British hotel be converted to this?

definitions.text: Could British hotel be converted to this?

indicators.note: a building converted is changed into something else, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a seedy British hotel might be turned into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be converted' rearranges BR plus HOTEL; the whole clue also hints at what such a hotel might become.
explanation.definitionFit: A disreputable hotel converted to rooms let by the hour would become a house of prostitution.

clue.text: Confusing passages in one of the Greek myths

definitions.meaning: the legend of Theseus and the Minotaur's maze in Crete

explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is a maze, and the most famous was Daedalus's in the Minotaur legend.

clue.text: Sailor coming to scrub cloth cap

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
scrub is low bushy vegetation, bush

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives to clean a fabric hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrub' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for scrubland, BUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarboosh is a brimless felt cap like a fez, worn in the Muslim world.

clue.text: Carriages taking time on the Central Line

parts.note: an axis is a central line through a body

explanation.surface: Trains running on London's Central Line take some time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central Line is a London Underground line, but here it is just a line through the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxis are hired cars, vehicles that carry passengers.

clue.text: Cultivated, as sugar often is

definitions.meaning: sugar is commonly purified into white crystals

explanation.definitionFit: Refined means both cultured in manners and purified by processing, as with sugar.

clue.text: Equity, for example, in old workhouse

definitions.meaning: Equity is the British actors' trade ...
under the Poor Law, parishes grouped into a ... ran a workhouse, itself called the ...

explanation.definitionFit: Union names both a trade union such as Equity and the Victorian workhouse.

clue.text: Sprinted round lair 'and stiffened

indicators.note: the running word goes round the lair word

parts.note: hared means ran fast
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: In dropped-aitch speech, someone ran round a hiding place and went rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and is a link word written as dropped-aitch speech for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened means made firm or rigid, so stiffened is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A growing case for decorating outside of flat?

definitions.text: A growing case for decorating outside of flat?

parts.words: A growing case for decorating outside of flat?
parts.note: a container in which plants grow, fixed on a window sill outside an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: A box of soil on a sill holds growing plants that decorate a home's exterior.

clue.text: Cook, say, associated with balsam

indicators.note: say signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: a fryer is one who cooks by frying

explanation.surface: A chef, perhaps, linked to a soothing resin.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar's balsam is an old inhalant remedy for colds; Cook also hints at Captain Cook, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar's balsam is a traditional benzoin inhalation, so the word goes with balsam.

clue.text: Charge on street removed as a ridiculous thing

indicators.note: the following words are taken out of the charge word

parts.note: an onslaught is a fierce attacking charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fee for street parking has been dropped, which seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee, but it is a military assault; the letters to go are not side by side, so they come out from separate places.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a joke or farce is called a laugh, a ridiculous thing.

clue.text: Right old error, to put stake on this horse

parts.note: a sin is a moral error
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler places a bet on a horse despite a correct old mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is Don Quixote's old nag in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocinante is the famous horse of Don Quixote, a proper name for a steed.

clue.text: In due course getting tired out recklessly seeking pleasure

parts.note: all in means exhausted
good-time describes someone pursuing pleasure regardless

explanation.surface: Eventually an exhausted person goes wild having fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, when the right moment comes.

clue.text: Place one's butt on the ground and demand charity, say

definitions.text: Place one's butt on the ground

parts.note: to order is to demand

indicators.note: say signals that the charity word is pronounced like another word

parts.note: alms are gifts given in charity

explanation.surface: A beggar sits down and asks for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech ALMS and ARMS sound the same. The butt is a rifle butt, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Order arms is the drill command to lower the rifle so its butt rests beside the foot.

clue.text: Broke in with answer."No trumps'

parts.note: taken as written
to solve is to answer a problem
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bridge player interrupts with an answer, bidding no trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke informally means having no money, unable to pay debts.

clue.text: In Mecca, aid demented professor

indicators.note: something demented is deranged, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: In the holy city a lecturer's assistant has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a university scholar, a senior member of academia.

clue.text: Sweep away the cards and prepare for action

definitions.meaning: literally removing playing cards from the deck surfaces of a table
on a warship, removing loose gear from the decks before battle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get ready for action, from warships emptying their decks before battle.

clue.text: Again request judge to drop case at the start

indicators.note: the judge word must lose the following letter

parts.note: a recorder is a part-time judge in English courts

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word case is taken

explanation.surface: A request to a judge to throw out a case right at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder is a barrister sitting as a part-time judge in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to place an order again, requesting the same goods once more.

clue.text: Aromatic plant found in estate, say, on a path

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, the British term for a station wagon
a way is a path

explanation.surface: A fragrant herb grows on a path through a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an estate car is a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is a herb of the parsley family grown for its aromatic seeds.

clue.text: Given some jostle, rebuking inn servant

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are given

explanation.surface: Someone shoved and then scolded the person who works at the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given some' takes the letters running across the words jostle and rebuking.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the stableman at an inn who looked after guests' horses.

clue.text: Lassie's appropriate indication of calling

parts.note: Lassie, the film collie, would aptly wear a pet's neckband; calling is also a vocation to the priesthood

explanation.definitionFit: A clerical white collar marks a priest's vocation and also names what a dog wears.

clue.text: Good rule broken when doing porridge

indicators.note: a rule broken is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A good rule is broken while serving a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing porridge is British slang for serving time in prison, which misdirects from the breakfast sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin porridge of oats boiled in water or milk.

clue.text: Native anaesthetic

definitions.meaning: a ... anaesthetic numbs only one part of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Local means native to a place and is short for a local anaesthetic.

clue.text: Standards in football

definitions.meaning: principles or regulations to be followed
Australian ... is a code of football, often called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Rules are standards to follow, and Rules is short for Australian Rules football.

clue.text: Fungus that can form a jelly

definitions.meaning: a furry growth on damp or old food
a shaped container in which a jelly sets

explanation.definitionFit: Mould is both a fungal growth and a shaped vessel in which a jelly sets.

clue.text: Mini revolution? It's about time for a sideways turn

indicators.note: the car and wheel words go round the time letter

parts.note: the Mini is a small car
a wheel is a turning revolution

explanation.surface: A small rotation, perhaps, is about to happen at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic British small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a gymnastic move in which the body turns sideways over the hands.

clue.text: Short hymn about love's dawning is hypnotic

indicators.note: the shortened hymn goes round the initial letter
short means cut, so the hymn word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chorale is a hymn tune

indicators.note: the dawning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief hymn about the beginning of love sends you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' turns CHORALE into CHORAL, which goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloral is a sedative drug, and hypnotic as a noun means a sleep-inducing drug.

clue.text: More cautious about the way unscrupulous lawyer appears

indicators.note: the cautious word is put round the way word

parts.note: shyer means more timid or wary
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A more careful person seems to be a crooked lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a disreputable person, especially a crooked lawyer.
